angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 45,832,716 km at 60.83 pc = 10.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 63090: distance 60.827 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.013), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 60.827 +/- 0.791 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 17.4065 +/- 0.2513 mas (same row, RUWE 2.76), 69.3 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 65.88 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 63090: radius 65.88 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 697.427 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.07) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 45,832,716 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 3657 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 63090: effective temperature 3657 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.171) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 63090: effective temperature 3657 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.171) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 112300 (pscomppars): spectral type M1 III, from Lee et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...678A.106L/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * del Vir: main object type RG*, Red Giant Branch star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 112300 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.06 dex, from Lee et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...678A.106L/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 112300 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 2.70121, from Lee et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...678A.106L/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 112300 (pscomppars): rotation period 4200 d, from Lee et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...678A.106L/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 112300 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 8.1 km/s, from Lee et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...678A.106L/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 0.8 from 2012ApJ...761..161S, the median of its 2 spectra; the 8 published values span log g 0.8 to 1.3, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.2% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2012ApJ...761..161S)
